work_or_witness: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring · Title header; Details; HISTORY
definition: The selected witness is Peter Jackson's 2001, 178-minute theatrical The Fellowship of the Ring, restricted to its prologue and early Shire departure sequence.
cultural_caution: This is a film-continuity and cut boundary. It excludes the books, extended-edition-only additions, later trilogy films, games, and other adaptations.

supports: 2001 release, 178-minute duration, New Line Cinema production, and the prologue-to-Shire film structure.

work_or_witness: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring · SYNOPSIS, prologue paragraphs 1–4 and Shire paragraph 2
definition: AFI describes a master Ring secretly forged by Sauron, with power to rule the other rings; the early witness identifies it as Sauron's and treats its possession as dangerous.
cultural_caution: The Ring is a fictional artifact and never a character endpoint. Its source-summary corruption, invisibility, and aging language is not mapped to real addiction, illness, disability, body change, morality, or spiritual doctrine.

citations.locator: SYNOPSIS, prologue paragraphs 1–4 and Shire paragraph 2
supports: Sauron's forging of the master Ring, its effects in the prologue, and Gandalf's identification of it in the Shire.

work_or_witness: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring · SYNOPSIS, prologue and Shire paragraphs
canonical_term: Hobbit, Elf, and other people/species descriptors
definition: AFI uses Hobbit, Elf lord, Hobbit-like creature, Orc, and Mortal Men in its film synopsis. In this pass those are source-native fictional people/species descriptors only.
cultural_caution: Do not map these terms to real race, ethnicity, nationality, caste, height, body, disability, or moral worth. The source's language about Orcs, corruption, or disfigurement does not establish good/evil essentialism.

supports: The cited fantasy people/species descriptors in the selected film synopsis.

work_or_witness: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring · SYNOPSIS, Shire and early Isengard paragraphs
definition: The early film synopsis calls Gandalf and Saruman wizards and gives Saruman an organizational head role; it does not define a transferable system of magic or religion.
cultural_caution: Wizard, order, dark side, and corruption are fictional narrative terms. They are not real religious, spiritual, occult, gender, age, or moral classifications.

citations.locator: SYNOPSIS, Shire and early Isengard paragraphs
supports: Gandalf and Saruman as wizards; Saruman as head of Gandalf's order.

work_or_witness: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring · SYNOPSIS, prologue through early Isengard paragraphs
canonical_term: Shire, Rivendell, Isengard, Mordor, and Mount Doom
definition: These are fictional locations named in the early prologue/Shire account: the Shire is Bilbo's home and the departure point; Gandalf directs Frodo toward Elrond's house in Rivendell; Saruman resides in Isengard; the prologue situates the Ring at Mordor and Mount Doom.
cultural_caution: These are fictional places and not character nodes or real geographic, ethnic, national, religious, or political correspondences.

citations.locator: SYNOPSIS, prologue through early Isengard paragraphs
supports: The selected locations and their bounded early-film contexts.

work_or_witness: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring · SYNOPSIS, prologue through early Isengard paragraphs; HISTORY, adaptation discussion
canonical_term: adaptation, body, violence, gender, and good/evil evidence boundary
definition: The selected official account describes prologue combat, death, imprisonment, Ring effects, gendered fantasy titles, and source-specific people/species terms. It does not license real-world race/species, disability/body, medical, gender-identity, violence/trauma, or good/evil-essentialist mappings, nor does it settle adaptation differences against books or other cuts.
cultural_caution: This boundary retains the film's fictional stakes while preventing a narrow adaptation witness from becoming a claim about real people, identities, bodies, harms, or moral categories.

citations.locator: SYNOPSIS, prologue through early Isengard paragraphs; HISTORY, adaptation discussion
supports: Film-level combat, Ring/body language, titles, source descriptors, and AFI's account that the screenplay made adaptation changes.
